kill_fact: There is no catalyst in the primary record, the route the parent actually describes is supply-negative, the seller is not forced on any underwritable clock, and the floor is not a floor. (1) NOT DATED, NOT BINDING. Between the Q1 filings of 29 April 2026 and today (28 July 2026) neither Bausch Health nor Bausch + Lomb has filed anything separation-related: no Form 10, no S-1 or 424B, no merger 8-K, no record date, no vote window. BHC's only 8-Ks in that window are Item 5.07 (annual meeting, 19 May 2026) and Item 5.02 (director resignation, 26 June 2026). The condition is self-referential and verbatim unchanged for four years: the B+L Separation 'is subject to the achievement of targeted debt leverage ratios and the receipt of any applicable shareholder and other necessary approvals' (BHC 10-Q, 29 April 2026), with the leverage target undisclosed, and BLCO's own 10-Q adds 'There can be no assurance that the Separation will be consummated, the form any such consummated Separation would take or that a Distribution or Sale Transaction will occur.' CFO Jean-Jacques Charhon on 29 April 2026 tied the decision to three self-judged variables - free cash flow 'between now and the end of 2027', post-LOE EBITDA, and the price obtainable for the stake - which is a window opening in 2028 at the earliest, not a date. The driver label 'Forced_divest_flow' is therefore not supported: nothing forces this seller inside any catalyst window. (2) THE ONE LIVE PROCESS IS DEAD AND THE PRESSURE WAS DEFERRED. The only process that reached price discovery was formally abandoned on 6 February 2025 ('the process is complete, and will not result in a transaction at this time'), and the 8 April 2025 refinancing - $4.4 billion of 10.000% senior secured notes due April 2032 plus a $3.0 billion term loan B due October 2030 - extended roughly $6.87 billion of 2025-2028 maturities into 2030-2032 and earned an S&P upgrade from CCC+ to B-. (3) THE MECHANISM IS UNCHOSEN AND ITS LIKELY FORM MARKS THE POSITION DOWN FIRST. The bull needs a clean Distribution that multiplies the roughly 46 million-share float about eight-fold and widens index eligibility; that is the branch management is least committed to. BLCO's 10-Q conditions only the Distribution on the leverage target, while the CFO framed the third variable as 'the average selling price we hope to get by monetizing our equity stake in BLCO in completing the separation, if that is the path we are going to be taking.' A staged sale of 310,449,643 shares into a 46 million-share float prints a discount before it prints any re-rating. (4) THE FLOOR HAS NO ASSET BEHIND IT. $11.80 is a multiple applied to equity carrying $5,094 million of principal debt against $268 million of unrestricted cash (plus $11 million restricted) at 31 March 2026, on a $71 million attributable quarterly net loss, $4,737 million of goodwill and $32 million of quarterly operating cash flow. No cash box, no break fee, no rival bid, no CVR, no recovery claim. The 52-week low is $13.09, so $11.80 has never been tested and nothing stops it. (5) THE TARGET IS AN ARTEFACT OF A DEAD BID. $26.97 is essentially the ~$25/share implied by the 2024 TPG/Blackstone approach that ended without a transaction, and it sits above the street's most bullish 12-month case of $21. Confirmed live quote at the 27 July 2026 close: $16.28 (+0.68%), day range $16.24-$16.535, 52-week range $13.09-$18.915, market cap $5.80 billion. A single-binary event with no dated trigger, an unchosen mechanism whose likely form is dilutive to the tape, and an unbacked floor on 4.6x-levered equity: the asymmetry does not survive.
corrections: MATERIAL 1 (NEW, 28 July 2026) - the dossier is unaware of the RED-C Phase 3 failure, which broke the second of the CFO's own three variables. In January 2026 Bausch Health's Phase 3 RED-C studies in liver cirrhosis missed, ending an approximately $2 billion pursuit of a Xifaxan successor; BHC shares fell about 12.4% over the sequence and the CEO offered no alternative post-LOE plan. Because the separation is expressly gated on post-LOE EBITDA and an undisclosed leverage target, a failed franchise-replacement bet pushes that gate FURTHER out of reach, not closer. Neither the bull nor the bear section of the dossier mentions RED-C at all. MATERIAL 2 (NEW, 28 July 2026) - the parent's own equity is materially weaker than the dossier states, which makes the floor-breaking tail live rather than remote. The dossier says BHC's market value is 'about $2.1 billion' against a stake 'worth roughly $5.2 billion'. Verified at the 27 July 2026 close: BHC $4.48, market cap $1.67 billion, 52-week range $4.33-$8.69 - within about 3% of its 52-week low and roughly 48% below its high, with a 50-day average of $5.00 and a 200-day of $5.86. The stake is 310,449,643 x $16.28 = $5.05 billion. So the negative stub is about -$3.4 billion, not -$3.1 billion, and more importantly the parent's equity is in a visible downtrend into a 2028 maturity-and-patent-cliff convergence. The dossier's own tail case - a parent restructuring turning the 88% block into estate property and a disorderly court-supervised disposal pushing BLCO through the floor on supply alone - is the single most likely path to $11.80, and it is being repriced upward by the market right now. The dossier treats it as a remote footnote. MATERIAL 3 - the Xifaxan first-filer date is wrong and it is load-bearing for the forcing function. The dossier states the April 2024 Federal Circuit ruling blocked 'the first generic filer until October 2029.' The October 2029 injunction attaches to the NORWICH First ANDA, and Norwich is not the first filer: BHC's Q1 2026 10-Q states 'the FDA remains enjoined from approving the Norwich First ANDA until October 2029,' while CEO Thomas Appio said on the 29 April 2026 call, 'We know we will have a generic entrant on 01/01/2028. Right now, today, Teva remains the first filer and has first-filer status.' The parent's cliff is roughly 17 months away, not three-plus years. This cuts FOR the proximity of the forcing function while falsifying the stated fact, and the CFO added that losing exclusivity before 01/01/2028 'would translate into the need to monetize some of our assets earlier than originally planned' - i.e. the realistic near-term path is a DISTRESSED monetisation, which is the supply-negative branch, not the clean spin the target assumes. MATERIAL 4 - 'five to six years of patience' and 'maturities pushed to 2031 and 2032' overstate the April 2025 relief, and the refinancing arithmetic does not reconcile. BHC's own maturity table at 31 March 2026 shows $701 million due 2027, $3,765 million due 2028 and $1,667 million due 2029 against $20,212 million of total debt obligations (the 31 December 2025 10-K table reads $58m/2026, $701m/2027, $4,240m/2028, $1,662m/2029, $4,118m/2030, $9,453m thereafter, total $20,232m). Roughly $4.5 billion still matures in 2027-2028, landing in the same year as the Xifaxan cliff - so the wall was DEFERRED, not removed, and the moderator's governing fact ('the pressure that would have forced the sale has been removed') is too strong. The correct instrument years are also not 2031-2032: the term loan B is due 8 October 2030 and the revolver 8 April 2030; only the $4.4 billion of notes run to April 2032. Separately, the dossier's '$7.9 billion refinancing' does not add up from its own components: $4.4 billion of notes plus a $3.0 billion term loan is $7.4 billion ($7.9 billion includes the $500 million revolver). The substance - 2025-2028 maturities materially extended and S&P raising BHC from CCC+ to B- with a negative outlook - is confirmed. Net effect on the thesis: the forcing function is REAL but dated to 2027-2028, which is outside any tradeable catalyst window and does not rescue an event-driven sleeve entry today. MATERIAL 5 - the fraudulent-transfer gate is REAL but is NOT disclosed in either company's Q1 2026 10-Q, and the solvency-opinion gate remains unsourced. The case is correctly captioned in the dossier: GMO Trust, et al. v. Bausch Health Companies Inc., No. SOM-C-12010-22, Superior Court of New Jersey, Chancery Division, Somerset County; in April 2023 Judge Margaret Goodzeit largely denied the motion to dismiss and expressly upheld the plaintiffs' right to enjoin BHC's proposed dividend of Bausch + Lomb shares. But there are zero occurrences of 'fraudulent', 'conveyance' or 'solvency' in either the BHC or the BLCO Q1 2026 10-Q (both filed 29 April 2026), and all five 'enjoin' hits in BHC's filing are Norwich/DRL patent injunctions. The litigation gate must therefore be cited to the state-court docket, not to the filings; no 2026 trial date or renewed injunction motion is publicly docketed. The SEPARATE claim that an independent solvency opinion is a Canadian closing condition contested by Apollo, Elliott and GoldenTree remains unverified against any primary source and should be struck or re-sourced. What BHC actually names as the gating consideration is different: it 'continues to evaluate all relevant factors and considerations related to completing the B+L Separation, including the Xifaxan Generics Litigation.' MATERIAL 6 - a live Xifaxan antitrust wave is missing from both sides of the dossier: direct- and indirect-purchaser class actions filed 7 October 2025 (Walgreen, Kroger, Albertsons, H-E-B, Supervalu), 21-23 October 2025 (KPH Healthcare, Value Drug) and 23 December 2025 (CVS Pharmacy) allege the Teva settlement and Orange Book listings for Xifaxan 550 mg were anticompetitive; CMS has separately selected Xifaxan for Medicare price negotiation effective 2027. Both compress post-LOE parent EBITDA alongside the RED-C failure. MATERIAL 7 - the risk/reward is mis-stated on the board entry: the 2.4:1 is computed against the event-win price as though it were the base case; measured against the parts value of about $20.25 with the event unscheduled, the honest base-case ratio is about 0.9:1. The dossier's own risk_reward field already says this - the board entry does not. MINOR - the header says 'BHC 88% overhang'; both 10-Qs say approximately 87% (310,449,643 of 356.5 million shares = 87.1%). MINOR - total debt is $5,094 million principal / $5,039 million carrying at 31 March 2026, not $5.07 billion, and the '$279 million of cash' is cash AND restricted cash ($268 million + $11 million); unrestricted cash is $268 million.
